pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🌐 **Strand 3 — Communication Networks**
Sub-strand 4: Web Technologies

A blog lets a person, a club or a school share news, ideas and achievements with the world. In this unit you will examine why blogs are important and create and publish a blog for your school or a club.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B9.3.4.1** Demonstrate the use of a web browser (blogging).

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B9.3.4.1.1** Examine the importance of creating blogs.
- **B9.3.4.1.2** Develop a blog for the school or a social club.
- **B9.3.4.1.3** Explore the steps in publishing a blog.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 11.1 The Importance of Blogs
- 11.2 Developing a Blog for the School or a Club
- 11.3 Publishing a Blog and Inviting Comments

**Core competencies developed:** Creativity and Innovation (CI6.6), Digital Literacy (DL5.3, DL6.3).

pages.title: The Importance of Blogs
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.3.4.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- define a blog;
- discuss the importance of creating blogs.
A **blog** (short for **weblog**) is a website made up of **posts** (articles) displayed in reverse date order, newest first. The writer is a **blogger**, and readers can usually leave **comments**. A **vlog** is a video blog.
- **Share information and news:** school events, club activities, results, announcements.
- **Improve writing and digital skills:** learners practise writing, editing and digital media.
- **Showcase achievements:** projects, competitions, art and poetry.
- **Build community:** parents, old students and the public can follow and comment.
- **Personal branding and careers:** blogs act as online portfolios.
- **Income:** popular blogs can earn money through advertising and sponsorship.
- **Free and easy:** platforms such as **Blogger**, **WordPress.com** and **Google Sites** need no coding.

pages.title: Developing a Blog for the School or a Club
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.3.4.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- investigate items to include in a school or club blog;
- develop the blog.
[[fig:c9-f13|Figure 12: Typical parts of a club blog]]
| **Item to include** | **Purpose** |
|---|---|
| Blog title and header image/logo | Identity of the school or club |
| About page | Who you are, your aims, your patron |
| Posts | News, reports of events, tutorials, project write-ups |
| Categories / labels | Organise posts (Events, Projects, Tips) |
| Gallery | Photos (with permission; avoid learners’ full names with faces) |
| Events calendar | Upcoming meetings and competitions |
| Contact page | Official school email, not personal phone numbers |
| Comment rules | Moderated comments; respectful language |
> 🪜 **Step by step — Creating a blog with Blogger (blogger.com)**
1. With your teacher, sign in to **blogger.com** using the school or club’s Google account.
2. Click **Create blog**, type a **title** (e.g. St. Mary’s JHS Computing Club), choose an available **address** (e.g. stmarysjhscomputing.blogspot.com) and click **Save**.
3. Click **Theme** and choose a design; click **Customise** to change colours and fonts.
4. Click **Layout** to add gadgets such as a header image, About Me, Labels and a Search box.
5. Click **Pages › New page** to create **About Us** and **Contact** pages.

pages.title: Publishing a Blog and Inviting Comments
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.3.4.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- identify the steps in publishing a blog;
- publish a post and invite others to comment.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Publishing a post**
1. Click **+ New Post**.
2. Type a clear **title** and write the post. Add pictures (**Insert image**), links and headings.
3. Add **labels** (e.g. Events), and under **Search description** write a short summary.
4. Click **Preview** to check the post, and proofread it.
5. Click **Publish** and confirm. The post is now live on the web.
6. Share the blog link on the school’s social media page or by email, and **invite readers to comment**.
7. Under **Settings › Comments**, choose who can comment and turn on **comment moderation** so that comments appear only after approval.
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Responsible blogging**
- Get the teacher’s approval before publishing.
- Protect privacy: no home addresses, phone numbers or full names of learners alongside photos.
- Respect copyright: use your own photos or free-to-use images and credit sources.
- Be truthful and respectful; moderate comments.
> 💻 **Practical session — Club blog project**
In groups, create a blog for your school or a club. Publish at least **three posts** (an introduction, an event report with photos, and a how-to tutorial), add an About page and a Contact page, share the link and respond politely to at least three comments.

pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. State **five** reasons why a school should have a blog.
2. List **six** items to include in a club blog.
3. Outline the steps for publishing a blog post and inviting comments.
